subChunks.title: Sizing — Width, Height, and Constraints
subChunks.hookHtml: Understanding how to size elements explicitly — and when to let content drive size — is the difference between layouts that hold together and layouts that break unpredictably. Tailwind's sizing utilities cover fixed sizes, fractions, viewport units, and the min/max constraints that keep responsive design sane.
subChunks.explanationHtml:
Width

/* Spacing scale (same as padding) */
w-0  w-1  w-2  w-4  w-8  w-16  w-32  w-64

/* Fractions */
w-1/2   /* 50%  */
w-1/3   /* 33.333% */
w-2/3   /* 66.667% */
w-1/4   /* 25%  */
w-3/4   /* 75%  */

/* Keywords */
w-auto    /* content width       */
w-full    /* 100% of parent      */
w-screen  /* 100vw               */
w-min     /* min-content         */
w-max     /* max-content         */
w-fit     /* fit-content         */

Height

h-0  h-1  h-2  h-4  h-8  h-16  h-32  h-64
h-auto    /* content height      */
h-full    /* 100% of parent      */
h-screen  /* 100vh               */
h-svh     /* 100svh (mobile fix) */
h-dvh     /* 100dvh (dynamic vh) */

Min and Max constraints

/* Minimum width/height */
min-w-0       /* 0 — important for flex-1 + truncate to work */
min-w-full    /* 100% */
min-h-screen  /* 100vh — full-page layouts */
min-h-0       /* 0 */

/* Maximum width/height */
max-w-xs  max-w-sm  max-w-md  max-w-lg  max-w-xl
max-w-2xl  max-w-4xl  max-w-7xl  max-w-prose  max-w-full
max-h-48  max-h-64  max-h-96  max-h-screen

Fixed sizes for icons and avatars

/* Common fixed square sizes */
w-4 h-4    /* 16px — small icon  */
w-5 h-5    /* 20px — icon        */
w-6 h-6    /* 24px — icon        */
w-8 h-8    /* 32px — small avatar */
w-10 h-10  /* 40px — avatar      */
w-12 h-12  /* 48px — avatar      */
w-16 h-16  /* 64px — large avatar */

Aspect ratio

aspect-square  /* 1 / 1  */
aspect-video   /* 16 / 9 */
aspect-auto

Object fit (for images)

object-cover    /* fills container, crops to fit */
object-contain  /* fits inside without cropping  */
object-fill     /* stretches to fill             */
object-center   /* centers the image             */

Master Ember: "min-w-0 is the most frequently forgotten utility in Tailwind. When you add flex-1 to a container hoping text will truncate, it won't — unless you also add min-w-0. The default min-width is auto (the content's natural width), which prevents shrinking below the text. Always pair flex-1 min-w-0 on containers that need to shrink."

storyBeats.speaker: Master Ember
storyBeats.text: Two patterns you will use on every avatar: the fixed square with rounded-full for circles, and object-cover to fill without stretching. w-12 h-12 rounded-full object-cover — that is every avatar in every app. Learn it once.

subChunks.soloPracticeHtml: Build a quest card: a landscape banner image (16:9 aspect, full width, object-cover), then a row with a 48px circular avatar, the quest title (truncated if too long), and an XP badge. The card should be constrained to max-w-sm and centred.
subChunks.feynmanPrompt: Explain why flex-1 alone is not enough for text truncation to work in a flex container — what is min-w-0, why is it needed, and what is the CSS mechanism behind the problem? When would you use w-full vs max-w-full?

questions.prompt: Which class constrains an image to maintain a 16:9 aspect ratio as it resizes?
questions.explanation: aspect-video applies aspect-ratio: 16 / 9. Combined with w-full and object-cover, this creates a responsive image that maintains its ratio at any container width. aspect-square does the same for 1:1 ratios.

questions.prompt: You add flex-1 to a div containing a long text string, hoping it will shrink and the text will truncate. It doesn't work. What is missing?
options: min-w-0 on the same element — flex items have min-width: auto by default, preventing shrinking below content width
questions.answer: min-w-0 on the same element — flex items have min-width: auto by default, preventing shrinking below content width
questions.explanation: CSS flex items have min-width: auto by default — they won't shrink smaller than their content. min-w-0 overrides this to allow shrinking. The full pattern for shrinkable text in flex: flex-1 min-w-0 on the container, then truncate on the text element.

questions.prompt: You need a full-page layout where the footer is always at the bottom of the viewport, and the main content area fills all remaining space. Which class combination achieves this?
options: min-h-screen flex flex-col on the root, flex-1 on the main element
h-screen overflow-scroll on the root, h-full on the main element
position-fixed on the footer, padding-bottom on the main element
h-full on the root, flex-grow on the main element
questions.answer: min-h-screen flex flex-col on the root, flex-1 on the main element
questions.explanation: min-h-screen ensures the root is at least full viewport height. flex flex-col makes it a vertical flex container. flex-1 on main makes it grow to fill all remaining space between the nav and footer. min-h-screen (not h-screen) allows the page to grow taller than the viewport if content requires it.
